candidate.name: Concourse
candidate.description: AI Agents for corporate finance teams
candidate.long_description: Concourse is building AI agents for corporate finance teams. Concourse works alongside finances teams to assist in day-to-day operations by taking on the most manual and time consuming work. Core to the platform is an AI analyst tailor-built for finance teams that is available at any hour of the day, accessible via natural language, and built with full connectivity to a company’s existing financial systems. Concourse enables team members to more effectively retrieve and analyze data, generate charts and reports, and answer ad-hoc questions.

score.thesis: AI-native autonomous agents owning high-value business workflows

analysis.team: Two founders. Matthieu Hafemeister was previously Head of Growth at Jeeves (YC S20) and a fintech investor at Andreessen Horowitz, giving relevant fintech and go-to-market background (Founder bio: Matthieu Hafemeister). Ted Michaels is the co-founder; no bio detail is provided in the sources, so his technical or domain depth is unknown (Founder bio: Ted Michaels). Team size is 7 (YC profile). No source material establishes who owns the technical/engineering leadership, which is an open question given the AI-native positioning.
analysis.product: Concourse builds AI agents for corporate finance teams. Per its own description, it works alongside finance teams to assist with day-to-day operations by taking on manual, time-consuming work (YC long description). The core is an AI analyst built for finance teams, available around the clock, accessible via natural language, and connected to a company's existing financial systems, enabling users to retrieve and analyze data, generate charts and reports, and answer ad-hoc questions (YC long description). Framing is explicitly assistive — it 'assists' and works 'alongside' teams rather than autonomously owning a workflow end to end.
analysis.market: The target market is corporate finance and accounting teams (tags: Finance and Accounting, Fintech, B2B SaaS). The sources give no market size, no customer names, no revenue, and no named competitors, so market scale and competitive positioning are unknown and cannot be assessed from the provided material. A why-now is only implied by the AI/agent positioning; no explicit timing thesis is stated in the sources.
risks: Assistive framing, not workflow ownership: the product 'assists' and works 'alongside' finance teams rather than autonomously owning a high-value workflow, which is the core of the thesis (YC long description).
No explicit autonomy: nothing in the sources describes the agent acting autonomously or taking irreversible actions without a human in the loop (YC long description).
Unknown market traction: no customers, revenue, retention, or market-size data are provided, so demand and scale are unverified (source material).

Unclear technical depth: no engineering/AI background is disclosed for co-founder Ted Michaels, and no product differentiation versus a generic finance copilot is described (Founder bio: Ted Michaels; YC long description).
what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence the agent autonomously executes and owns finance workflows end to end (e.g. closes the books, runs reconciliations) rather than answering ad-hoc questions.
Traction proof: named enterprise finance customers, revenue, or retention showing high-value workflow adoption.
Demonstrated technical differentiation and defensibility over generic natural-language finance assistants, plus clearer evidence of AI/engineering depth on the founding team.
analysis.recommendation_rationale: Concourse scores strongly on AI centrality but weakly on the thesis core: its own description frames the product as assistive — working 'alongside' finance teams to 'assist' — rather than autonomously owning a high-value workflow, and no autonomy language is present (YC long description). Combined with no disclosed traction, market size, or clear technical differentiation, the evidence does not support the autonomous-agent thesis at this stage. Consistent with the 37/100 weak score, we recommend Pass, while noting the credible fintech go-to-market background of one founder as a reason to revisit if autonomy and traction are demonstrated.
